newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Golden Valley rejects Bre-X statement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Golden Valley rejects Bre-X statement.

text.p: Australia's Golden Valley Mines NL said it on Thursday emphatically rejected the suggestion by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd that Golden Valley made a false and misleading statement in saying it was entitled to part of the huge Busang gold prospect in Indonesia.
In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Golden Valley said Bre-X's allegations were without foundation.

On Monday, Golden Valley said it had teamed up in a technical assistance and finance agreement with PT Krueng Gasui, which has a 10 percent interest in the Muara Atan Contract of Work (COW), which contains part of the Busang deposit.

Tracing the background of the project, Golden Valley said the Indonesian partner was seeking a ruling from the Indonesian government that the Muara Atan COW should be extended to include adjoining areas including the Busang South East Zone.

The effect of this would be to give both PT Krueng Gasui and PT Sungai Atan Perdana, the other Indonesian 10 percent partner in the COW, which Golden Valley has also agreed to assist on similar terms, a stake in the whole of the Busang deposit.
Golden Valley said PT Krueng Gasui also has an option over a further 20 percent interest in the Muara Atan COW which is now held by a subsidiary of Bre-X.

Golden Valley said Busang was discovered in 1988 when the Perth-based Montague/Westralian Group was the foreign partner in the COW and that Bre-X took over as operator after a deal with Westralian in July 1993.

Bre-X reported to the Toronto Stock Exchange last April that Busang contains a gold resource of 622 million tonnes at an average grade of 2.34 grams a tonne for 46.92 million ounces of contained gold, it said.
Most of this resource is reported to be contained in the south-easterly extension of the ore-body over which Bre-X has applied for a new COW, Golden Valley said.

Last July PT Krueng Gasui told the Indonesian government and Bre-X that its exclusion from the new COW application covering the South East Zone was unfair and was in breach of Bre-X's duties as operator of the joint venture and the articles of the COW, Golden Valley said.

"The position of PT Krueng Gasui as submitted to the Indonesian Government is that the Indonesian partners ought to have been included in the applications for new COWs covering the adjoining areas and Bre-X's failure to do so was for its own advantage rather than for the benefit of the joint venture of which it was manager and operator," Golden Valley said.
"Bre-X's allegations are clearly without foundation as there is ample evidence in the public domain to support the Indonesian partners' position," Golden Valley said.

The call option has been a matter of public record, included in all the relevant annual reports of publicly-listed Montague Gold NL and Westralian Resource Projects Ltd in Australia from 1987 to 1994, it said.

"In light of this, it is incomprehensible to the Indonesian partners and Golden Valley why Bre-X has failed for the last three years to inform the market in Canada of the existence of this agreement," Golden Valley said.

"PT Krueng Gasui has obtained advice on both Indonesian and Canadian law and has presented its position that Bre-X has acted in breach of its fiduciary duties as operator of the Muara Atan joint venture and has failed to observe a number of the important terms of the Contract of Work with the Indonesian government and the laws of the Republic of Indonesia," it added.
Bre-X said on Tuesday it has requested the ASX to ask Golden Valley to back up its claims.
Bre-X shares fell sharply in Toronto on Wednesday on news of the dispute over Busang.
